### Summary

kintera computes in SI units with amounts in moles. Input data often come in other units, such as rate constants
in molecule, cm and s. The `Units` and `UnitSystem` classes parse a unit string, check its dimensions and convert a
value to kintera's base units. The physical constants every module shares are defined once in one header.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Convert a value from a unit string to SI-and-mole, @eq-ch02-units-factor.

**Data.** A value and a unit string such as `cm^3/molecule/s` in; the value in kg, m, s, K, A, mol out.

**Placement.** Used by the reaction readers (`arrhenius`, fall-off, evaporation) when they read YAML.

**Activation.** Always for those readers; base units are kg, m, s, mol, Pa, J, K, A.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact factor products; dimension check on conversion.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $f_u$, the conversion factor of a base unit $u$ to SI [-]; $p_u$, its prefix factor [-]; $k_u$, its exponent in the unit string
[-]; $f$, the factor of the whole unit [-]; $N_{\mathrm A}$, the Avogadro constant [mol$^{-1}$].

### Derivation

A unit string is a product of base units with exponents, each base unit optionally carrying an SI prefix. Its
factor to SI is the product

$$
f = \prod_u \left(p_u f_u\right)^{k_u} ,
$$ {#eq-ch02-units-factor}

where the prefix factor $p_u$ is, for example, $10^{-2}$ for `c`, and the base-unit factor $f_u$ is, for example,
$1/N_{\mathrm A}$ mol for `molecule`. The value in base units is the value times $f$. The parser in the `Units`
constructor ({{< code src/units/units.cpp Units::Units overload=2 >}}) splits the string at `*` and `/`, reads each
exponent after `^`, looks the name up among the known units first and only then tries a one-letter prefix, so `m` is
the metre and `mm` the millimetre.

The shared constants are, in `src/constants.h` ({{< code src/constants.h >}}): $N_{\mathrm A} = 6.02214076 \times
10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\mathcal R = 8.31446$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, $k_{\mathrm B} = 1.380649 \times 10^{-23}$
J K$^{-1}$, $e = 1.602176634 \times 10^{-19}$ C and 1 atm $= 101325$ Pa. $N_{\mathrm A}$, $k_{\mathrm B}$ and $e$ are
the exact SI values. $\mathcal R$ is truncated: $N_{\mathrm A} k_{\mathrm B} = 8.314462618\ldots$ J mol$^{-1}$
K$^{-1}$, so the stored value is smaller by $2.6 \times 10^{-6}$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, a relative
$3.1 \times 10^{-7}$ (arithmetic on the constants as printed).

### Numerical method

No numerical method: one product of factors per conversion.

The units figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of units and constants. {#tbl-ch02-units-code}

Setup checks a user can hit, each an `std::invalid_argument` from `units.cpp`: "Unknown unit" for a name that is
neither a known unit nor a prefix plus one; "Cannot convert from ... to ..." for units of different dimensions;
"not supported for temperature" or "for current" for a unit the system cannot take for that dimension; and "does
not represent unity conversion factor" when a factor of one is required.

### Limits

$\mathcal R$ and $N_{\mathrm A} k_{\mathrm B}$ differ by a relative $3.1 \times 10^{-7}$, so a quantity converted
once through $k_{\mathrm B}$ and once through $\mathcal R$ disagrees at that level. Whether any code path mixes the two
is not checked here.
